numeral.purpose: Round numbers, shelf counts, days-left clock; in the track's ink where a track owns it.

display.purpose: A single winner's cover headline and banner hero names; 3.75rem phone to 5.75rem desktop.

headline.purpose: Page titles on a 2px paper rule; 3rem to 3.75rem.

title.purpose: Section headings on a 2px paper rule; panel titles 1.45-2rem.

body.purpose: Blurbs and reviews, 48-68ch measure, tabular numerals.

label.purpose: Nav, buttons, running head, stats captions, meta; tracked condensed caps.

shadows.name: object-lift

shadows.name: type-on-art

shadows.name: inset-ring
shadows.purpose: Stroke without layout shift; yellow marks a selection, rule-strong or paper-mute for neutral strokes.

shadows.name: die-cut-rest
shadows.purpose: An unlocked icon resting on its slot; up to 0 8px 16px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55) for fanned icons and pinned Highlights.

shadows.name: gutter-shade
shadows.purpose: Binder and spread pages darkening into the gutter (mirrored on the facing page; 22px/26px/-20px on the spread).

shadows.name: tab-lift
shadows.purpose: A binder index row's tint tab standing proud of the binder edge.

motion.name: burst-stamp
motion.purpose: The starburst stamps in once per page from 1.5x scale and 14deg off-tilt; motion-safe only.

motion.name: ease-art
motion.purpose: Key art scale on hover (1.03-1.04 over 500-700ms) and progress fills.

motion.name: landing-marquee
motion.value: linear infinite, pace set per cover
motion.purpose: The landing's foot of GOTM covers; pauses on hover or focus; still scrollable row under reduced motion.

motion.name: icon-straighten
motion.purpose: An unlocked icon straightens from its stable tilt (within 1.5deg) on hover; motion-safe only.

gradients.name: foil
gradients.purpose: The single sanctioned gradient: Platinum, Mastery and Completion only (stamp, die-cut edge, Platinum tier dot, club-page Platinum frame, margin signatures). Ink type; never on text.

gameTint.source: Vivid dominant hue of the set's cover (else set icon), sampled server-side; clamped to s 0.35-0.75, l 0.32-0.62, darkened until ink or paper clears 4.5:1.
gameTint.uses: Spine (10-14px), solid title band, view/index tabs, slot numbers and dots, progress bar, hidden-tile seal.
gameTint.exemption: Game art is content: exempt from the One Ink Per Track Rule.

newsInks.surfaces: News page, its cards and filter, category switches on /settings

narrative.overview:
Every Game of the Month round is an issue of the club's own 90s game magazine. The GOTM winner is the cover story, the Non-RPG pick is the feature, the club's open business (nominations, the vote) is a highlighter-yellow insert, and every other page is a department: GOTM history is the archive, a member's profile is their bookcase, a game page is its own cover story. The voice is loud and printed: ink-black stock, condensed caps set big, three spot inks that each mean one thing.

Density is magazine density, not dashboard density. A page leads with one monumental object (a round number, a game's two-line headline, a member's name in Anton at banner scale), then settles into ruled departments with labels in tracked condensed caps. Surfaces are hard rectangles with barely-there corners. Depth comes from key art under black legibility scrims, not from glowing cards.

The world refuses the default dark game-tracker: gradient-faded key-art cards, glow accents, gradient text. The app is dark-only (`<html class="dark">`, theme colour #0b0b0d).

**The Achievement Hub department.** Achievements are the magazine's collectors' department. A member's achievements are a binder opened on its gutter, each Achievement Set is a page or a two-page spread inside it, and the community hub is a wall of the club's Unlocks pinned up under paper-tape day labels. The department keeps the ink ground, Anton and Barlow, and the 2px paper rules, and it brings its own colour roles (game tint, Rarity inks, Provider colours, foil) that appear on achievement surfaces only. The binder refuses the tracker default of a stats header over a grid of progress cards. Icons are die-cut objects resting in slots, locked Achievements are dashed numbered slots, and hidden ones are sealed tiles.

**The News Hub department.** The club's news is the magazine's contact sheet. Every News Item is a frame of its art marked in its News Category's ink, and the frames are laid out by UTC day under Anton day headings. The department keeps the ink ground, Anton and Barlow, and the 2px rules, and it brings one colour role of its own (the News inks) that appears on news surfaces only. It refuses the news-site headline list and the dashboard default of stats over a wall of cards.
keyCharacteristics: Ink-black ground with three spot inks: masthead red for GOTM, violet for NR-GOTM, highlighter yellow for the member's own business.
Anton in caps for every headline and numeral, Barlow Condensed tracked caps for every label, Barlow for reading.
Monumental numerals: the round number, a shelf's count, the days-left clock.
The winner starburst, stamped once, only on winners.
Two-line game headlines, with the second line in the track's accent.
Hard rectangles (2-4px corners) and 2px paper rules under headings.
In the Achievement Hub: game-tint spines, bands and tabs; die-cut icons edged in their Rarity ink; foil stamps only for Platinum, Mastery and Completion.
In the News Hub: frames of art with a foot bar and a corner tag in the News Category's ink.

rules.name: The One Ink Per Track Rule
rules.body: Red means GOTM, violet means NR-GOTM, and nothing decorative borrows either. A GOTM element never wears violet and an NR element never wears red. A game that won both tracks reads as GOTM first.

rules.name: The Yellow Is Yours Rule
rules.body: Highlighter yellow is filled only for calls to action and the GOTM starburst. As type it marks the GOTM headline's second line and interaction states (hover, focus, selection, caret). It never fills a decorative panel.

rules.name: The Red Is Also Here Rule
rules.body: Besides GOTM, masthead red marks where you are: the active sidebar item and the running-head separators. It marks nothing else, with one sanctioned exception on the staff desk: the Off state of a Feature Flag (see the Off Red Rule).

rules.name: The Game Art Is Content Rule
rules.body: A game tint is sampled from the game's own art, so, like key art, it is exempt from the One Ink Per Track Rule: a red or violet tint never means GOTM or NR-GOTM. The system's own tints (the hashed fallbacks) stay off red and violet so a game without art never reads as a track.

rules.name: The Tint Carries Its Type Rule
rules.body: A tint never travels without its contrast colour. Type on a tint is ink or paper, whichever clears AA, and a tint band is always solid, never a gradient.

rules.name: The Foil Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Foil is the system's single sanctioned gradient. It marks only Platinum, Mastery and Completion: the foil stamp, the foil die-cut edge on the Unlock behind one, the Platinum tier dot, the foil frame behind a Platinum on a game's club page, and a Completion signed in the margin. It never sets text, and it never decorates.

rules.name: The Journal Ink Is a Person Rule
rules.body: A journal ink means one member and nothing else. The inks stay off masthead red, feature violet, highlighter yellow and signal orange, so a journal line never reads as a track, a call to action or a destructive action, and the yellow ring on a selected dot stays the only interaction mark. They do not borrow the Achievement roles (the member ring colours stay on achievement surfaces), and they never leave journal surfaces.

rules.name: The News Inks Stay on News Surfaces Rule
rules.body: A News ink means one News Category and nothing else, and it never leaves news surfaces. The inks do not borrow or lend to the Achievement roles or the Journal member inks: magenta sits near rarity-ultra and teal near the RetroAchievements Provider colour, but they never share a surface, so neither can be misread. Read them through `newsInk()` in lib/news.ts, which also says when to dash.

rules.name: The Two-Line Headline Rule
rules.body: A game's title breaks at its subtitle colon ("Metaphor:" / "ReFantazio"). Without a colon it breaks before the last word, and a one-word title is all second line. The second line takes the track's accent: yellow for a GOTM winner, soft violet for an NR-GOTM winner, paper for everything else. Every page that sets a game's name as a headline uses this one rule.

rules.name: The Caps Are the Face Rule
rules.body: Anton and Barlow Condensed are always set in caps through the `font-headline` and `font-label` utilities. Anton never sets mixed case, and it never sets body text.

rules.name: The Earned Over Total Rule
rules.body: In the Achievement Hub a count reads as an Anton numeral with its total beside it in paper-mute ("23 / 41"): a set header sets it at numeral scale, the binder index and club pages at 1.25-1.5rem. A member's Unlocks are the binder's monumental numeral (4.5rem to 5.25rem), with Completions, Masteries, Platinums and RA points as 2rem Anton over label captions. Slot numbers are two-digit Anton ("07").

rules.name: The Empty Track Rule
rules.body: A track with no winner gives its space away rather than apologising for it. On the dashboard, with no NR-GOTM the yellow round panel takes the whole right column at full height and lists the latest nominations. With no GOTM, the NR-GOTM is promoted to the cover in violet, with one small "No Game of the Month this round" note under the numeral. In the GOTM history ledger, where rows must align, an absent track keeps its column as a dashed rule-strong box with a short muted label. Under a title search, that box stays silent, because absence there means "no match".

rules.name: The Multi-Winner Rule
rules.body: Co-winners share one cover, never a carousel. Two winners split it (1.42fr / 1fr). Three put a tall lead panel beside two stacked panels (1.3fr / 1fr). The lead carries the numeral, a paper "N winners" tag and every outbound link, and the narrow panels keep two links. Each winner gets a square letter tile (A, B, C) in its track's ink, and titles step down by panel size. The NR rail does the same: one winner is a feature card, and two or three are a ranked list of covers with A/B/C letters. Side-by-side panels reserve equal blurb height so their stats and actions sit level.

rules.name: The Open Binder Rule
rules.body: A member's achievements open as a binder: a rule-coloured cover with 4px corners and a deep object lift, holding two ink-2 pages. From `xl` it is a 25rem left page (the member, their totals, Linked Accounts and four rarest Unlocks), a 30px gutter of rings, and the index page. Filter tabs (status, then one per Linked Account's Provider) sit on the binder's top edge, and each index row's game-tint tab sticks out past the binder's right edge. Below `xl` the binder closes to one page with the member first and the index below.

rules.name: The Spread Rule
rules.body: A set page is a two-page spread: from `xl` the left page (1.7fr) holds the view (Checklist, Rarity or Timeline) and the right page (at least 20rem) holds the picked Achievement's details over the Rarity tally, sticky under the top bar. The pages meet at a shadowed gutter. Game-tint view tabs sit on the spread's top edge. On phones the spread closes to one page and the details open under the picked item.

rules.name: The Day Band Rule
rules.body: The hub runs newest first in UTC day bands, each headed by a paper-tape label with a rule running out to its tally. From `xl` the Latest wall takes 62% beside a 38% rail of this week's Highlights. The wall is two columns from `sm`, and a card holding a Highlight spans both, as does a day's odd card out, so the wall never ends on a hole. The Highlights wall alone runs 2 to 6 columns without day bands, each tag carrying its own date.

rules.name: The Contact Sheet Rule
rules.body: The News page puts a 15.5rem category rail beside the card grid from `lg`, sticky under the top bar, with a 28px gap. Below `lg` the rail becomes a "Filter" outline-button disclosure above the grid holding the same list. The grid runs newest first in UTC day bands: each is headed by an Anton title ("Today", "Yesterday", or a date like "Sun 8 Nov", with the year added when it is not this year), a label-type date and item count in paper-mute, and a 2px rule-strong line running out to the edge. The grid's columns follow the width of its own column (a container query, not the viewport): one, then two, then three, with 20px gaps. Numbered pagination sits under the last band, followed by a small label-type "Days and times in UTC" note.

rules.name: The Scrim Not Glow Rule
rules.body: Key art is darkened from where the type sits (from the left for a single cover, from the foot for split panels) with ink gradients (`rgb(11 11 13 / 0.96 to 0.15)`). Art is never faded into a coloured gradient, and nothing glows.

rules.name: The Die-Cut Rule
rules.body: Achievement icons are die-cut objects, so they alone round to 6px (`rounded.die-cut`). The ring frame around a tile on a game's club page follows the cut at 7-8px. Everything else in the Achievement Hub keeps the hard rectangle: chips and stamps at 2px, tabs and tint bands at about 3.2px, the binder cover at 4px. Its round forms are the slot dots, the member ring dots, the PSN tier dot and avatars.

rules.name: The Hand-Placed Rule
rules.body: Objects that sit on the page rest at a tilt and pages stay square. An unlocked icon takes a stable tilt from its id (within ±1.5deg) and straightens on hover. A foil stamp is pressed at -8deg, an odds tag at 6deg, a day tape at about 1deg alternating, and a hand of fanned icons leans by position. A hidden tile is sealed by a diagonal band in the game tint, and a day tape has torn edges.

rules.name: The Desk Green Rule
rules.body: Done green (`ok`) shares the hex of the uncommon Rarity ink because the two never meet: Rarity inks stay on achievement surfaces and done green stays on the staff desk, which shows no achievements. It is its own token so neither role borrows the other, and it is still a mark (type, a stamp outline, a dot), never a fill behind type.

rules.name: The Off Red Rule
rules.body: On the staff desk only, masthead red also marks a Feature Flag that is Off: its selected segment and its state in the last change, as type and a stroke on ink (ink, not ink-3, under it, so the red clears 4.5:1). Off is the loudest thing a flag can do, so it takes the loudest ink, and staff alone see it, so it can never read as GOTM to a member. The confirmed action that turns a Feature Off is still a signal-orange destructive button: red is the state, orange is the act. Members' surfaces never show a flag's state.

dos: **Do** colour a thing red only if it is GOTM, "you are here" or (on the staff desk) an Off Feature Flag, violet only if it is NR-GOTM, and fill it yellow only if it is a call to action or the GOTM starburst.
**Do** open every page with one monumental object (a numeral or a two-line Anton headline) and rule every heading with 2px paper.
**Do** set every game headline with the Two-Line Headline Rule.
**Do** give an absent track's space to what remains (the yellow panel or the promoted NR cover) on the dashboard.
**Do** split one cover between co-winners and letter them A, B, C in the track's ink.
**Do** fall back to the title in Anton on ink-3 when art is missing.

**Do** keep motion to the single starburst stamp, gentle art scale on hover (1.03-1.04, 500-700ms), the landing marquee and, in the Achievement Hub, an icon straightening from its tilt on hover (200ms), all behind `motion-safe`.
**Do** keep the Achievement Hub's colour roles (game tint, Rarity inks, Provider colours, foil) on achievement surfaces, and set every tint with its contrast type.
**Do** keep foil for Platinum, Mastery and Completion.
**Do** use the glossary in achievement copy: Achievement, Achievement Set, Unlock, Highlight, Rarity, Completion, Mastery, Platinum, Provider, Linked Account.
**Do** keep the News inks on news surfaces (the News page, its cards and filter, the category switches on /settings), as foot bars, tags and squares with ink type, and always draw Rumours dashed.
donts: **Don't** fade key art into coloured gradients, add glow accents, or use gradient text. Foil is the single sanctioned gradient, and it never sets text.
**Don't** put a starburst on anything but a GOTM or NR-GOTM winner.
**Don't** put a breadcrumb inside a page; the running head is the only trail.
**Don't** add a small tracked-caps kicker or eyebrow above a headline. Track labels sit with a pick's art as data, not above titles as decoration.
**Don't** use hard offset shadows; shadows here are soft, black and directional.
**Don't** use emoji or text glyphs as icons; icons are line SVGs (Lucide) at 16-18px.
**Don't** set Anton in mixed case or at body sizes, or set body copy in Barlow Condensed.
**Don't** round corners past 4px except avatars, status dots and die-cut achievement icons (6px).
**Don't** put violet or GOTM red on an achievement surface; a game tint that happens to be red or violet is content, not a track.
**Don't** say sticker, album, pack or pull in the UI. The binder is a visual metaphor; the copy keeps the glossary terms.
**Don't** use done green or the desk stamps outside the staff desk, or red for a destructive action.
**Don't** fill a panel with a News ink, or use one on a surface that is not about news.
